subject: Traffic escape clause & automatic autorecover for Novacorp canary
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: traffic escape clause + autorecover for Novacorp canary

Team —

Novacorp is scheduled to begin a phased canary next week (see deal: DEAL-2027-0914-NOVA). They have a strict uptime/latency SLA we committed to in the contract (P95 latency <200ms, availability 99.95%). Given the expected traffic spike and the new quantized model variant we're rolling, legal and CS want an approved operational mitigation: an automated escape clause that does the following when gating thresholds are breached:

- Immediate fallback to the previous stable model variant for the affected region
- Pin the traffic to the stable variant for a configurable hold window (suggest 2 hours) or until manual release
- Emit an incident and notify customer-facing stakeholders + the customer via the existing webhook
- Auto-credit policy: if fallback is used for >30 minutes total across a day, finance will trigger a credit review (we'll coordinate separately)

Attachments: I uploaded a draft gate definition (canary_gate_definitions.yaml) and the signed SLA-exception form.

Asking for: operational sign-off (infra + runtime), confirmation that we can implement the fallback as an atomic action (no partial routing states), and approval on the pin window. Also need a short runbook for on-call.

Naomi
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: traffic escape clause + autorecover for Novacorp canary

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear ask. A few technical notes from runtime/serving side: 

1) Gate triggers: P95 > 200ms OR 5xx error rate > 0.5% over a 5-minute rolling window are reasonable starting points. Recommend a two-stage trigger:
   - Soft trigger (1 min sustained breach): send alert and start prefilling KV caches for stable variant.
   - Hard trigger (5 min sustained): execute fallback.

2) Pin semantics: we should support both soft-pin (route only new sessions to pinned variant, let in-flight requests drain) and hard-pin (immediate re-route including new requests). Hard-pin for Novacorp is fine but we should implement graceful drain for in-flight long-running responses.

3) Auto-unpin: instead of fixed 2 hours, propose auto-unpin when metrics return within threshold for a sustained 30-minute window, with a max 4-hour forced unpin to avoid permanent lock. Manual override must be available.

4) Observability hooks: add a telemetry tag for fallback_reason and include model_version metadata in every emitted metric. We'll need a quick schema change to the tracing payload (low-risk).

I can take the lead on implementing the gating rules and the telemetry changes. Will attach a minimal canary_gate_definitions.yaml with these thresholds.

—Aditya
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: traffic escape clause + autorecover for Novacorp canary

Thanks — this reads well. A few commercial constraints to note from the Novacorp negotiations: 

- They expect an explicit SLA escalation flow when the platform initiates automatic fallback. We should include a templated notification (tone + content) for legal and CS review.
- Novacorp asked that any forced pin windows longer than 1 hour require an explicit customer notification and acceptance of reduced feature exposure (we agreed to keep them informed).
- If fallback is used repeatedly (>3 times in a 30-day rolling window) the deal requires an executive review and potential service credits.

My ask: infra/runtime to confirm the notification hooks and make the pin window configurable per-customer (not hard-coded). Also please add the runbook steps Naomi requested and include the communications template.

I'll coordinate with CS/legal on the notification template once we have the technical hooks.

—Lauren
Director, Strategic Accounts
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novacorp.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: traffic escape clause + autorecover for Novacorp canary

Thanks, Aditya and Lauren — I like the two-stage trigger and the auto-unpin logic. Two items for Dylan: can you confirm that the routing layer can do an atomic variant swap (no split-brain routing) and that we can expose per-customer pin-window configuration in the console or via API? Also need a short runbook (5 bullets) we can attach to the SLA-exception form for audit.

If Dylan confirms, I approve moving forward with the following concrete defaults for Novacorp (we'll make them configurable):
- Soft trigger: P95 > 200ms sustained 1 minute
- Hard trigger: P95 > 200ms OR 5xx > 0.5% sustained 5 minutes
- Pin behavior: hard-pin with graceful drain; auto-unpin after 30 minutes of healthy metrics or max 4 hours
- Customer notification: immediate alert + templated email, CC exec-ops if pin > 1 hour

Naomi
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novacorp.com>, platformops@novacorp.com
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: traffic escape clause + autorecover for Novacorp canary

All — confirmed. Routing control can perform an atomic model swap within the region; we'll coordinate a 10s handoff window to allow graceful KV-cache warming on the stable variant. Per-customer pin configuration will be available via console API; I'll send a short runbook and the implementation PR.

PR/Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INFRA-2784
Runbook (brief):
1) Triage alert from canary gating channel (PagerDuty)
2) Verify metrics and trigger reason in telemetry dashboard
3) If hard trigger satisfied, execute atomic swap via routing API and set pin with reason tag
4) Notify CS/legal via templated message and CC customer; open incident in Ops
5) Monitor metrics; if auto-unpin condition met, unpin and run post-mortem if fallback occurred

I've attached canary_gate_definitions.yaml to the Jira PR and uploaded a signed SLA-exception-form_20270914.pdf to the deal folder.

—Dylan
Principal Infra Engineer
